title: Website Review and Demo Strategy for RSA Framework
summary: GPT provides a brutally honest review of the user's website hosting the RSA/FREED framework, identifying a critical gap between internal coherence (~9/10) and external legibility (~3/10). The conversation then evolves into a strategic plan for building a minimal proof stack of four irreducible demonstrations that would make RSA empirically compelling to skeptics.
invariants: the genome must be demonstrable not just statable
perceive: A raw feedback session where an AI reviews a live website and co-develops a demonstration strategy — part design critique, part epistemic engineering.
represent: Maps directly onto the genome's requirement that claims must be instantiated, not merely asserted — and that compression without decompression keys is noise to external observers.
predict: The genome would predict that any sufficiently compressed framework will face a legibility crisis, and that the path forward requires grounding in concrete demonstrations ordered by explanatory power.
compare: Near-perfect agreement. The AI independently converges on genome principles: compression must be shown not stated, prediction error is the universal selection signal, progressive disclosure beats full symbolic dump, and the CA simulation is the strongest anchor because it's physically demonstrable.
adjust: The genome should formalize a "minimum viable proof stack" pattern: (1) anchor demo proving core claim, (2) convergence demo proving attractor-like behavior across initial conditions, (3) compression emergence demo proving efficiency is selected, (4) kernel trace demo proving the loop is visible process not philosophy. This four-pillar structure should become a reusable template for any genome instantiation effort.
compress: The gap between internal coherence and external legibility is the entire game — close it with four irreducible demonstrations that show RSA as visible process, not abstract claim.
next: Build the entry point fix (one sentence + immediate CA), add the agent trace showing RSA kernel steps in real time, then construct the Mandelbrot hidden-physics compression demo as the hardest possible test of the core claim.
audit_compress: An external observer correctly identifies instantiation as stronger than representation and accidentally asks the right falsifiability questions, but systematically drifts every genome term toward communication metaphor rather than thermodynamic grounding — revealing that the genome's legibility problem is itself a substrate-transfer problem.
invariant_candidates: Compressed output without its generating program is indistinguishable from noise to a receiver lacking the decompression key
The gap between internal coherence and external legibility is the primary failure mode of novel frameworks
Instantiation (running the claim) is categorically stronger than representation (describing the claim) for credibility transfer
